Pebble Diary is a private diary for one family. The aim is to write something down quickly and find that day again later. People can sign in, change their settings, keep private diaries, and write entries. After sign-in they see today, and they can move to another day.

Read this for: how a person signs in, how long the session lasts, and what happens when they change their email or password. Source files: apps/accounts/views.py, apps/accounts/forms.py, apps/accounts/urls.py, apps/accounts/admin.py, apps/accounts/services/mail.py, apps/accounts/axes.py, config/settings.py, templates/registration/, apps/accounts/templates/accounts/settings.html, apps/accounts/templates/accounts/privacy.html Sign-in is email and password. The stored email is lowercase, and the sign-in form lowercases the address before it checks the password. A wrong password and an unknown email show the same error. Templates for sign-in and password reset live in templates/registration/. Settings live in accounts/settings.html. LoginRequiredMiddleware sits after the authentication middleware. A view is private unless it is marked with login_not_required. Sign-in, sign-out, password reset, registration, and the privacy page are marked. Everything else, including a view added later, redirects to sign-in. Admin views set their own login URL, so a signed-out request for /admin/ goes to the admin sign-in page. Sign-in lands on /, which redirects to today's day page. That page is on HTMX and templates.

A normal session lasts 14 days from the last visit. SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST refreshes that clock on each response. The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Production also marks it Secure. The sign-in form has This is a shared device. When it is checked, the view calls session.set_expiry(0). The cookie then has no expiry date, so the session ends when the browser closes. That session does not keep a browser draft. Drafts are on Entries and autosave. Sign-out is a POST. GET is not allowed.

The reset form always redirects to the same done page, whether or not an account uses that email. Mail is sent only when an active account with a usable password exists. The done page does not repeat the address. PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT is one hour. The link is Django's password-reset token. It stops working once the password changes, including when the same link is opened again, and it stops working after the hour. Setting the password sends a notice to the account email and signs out other sessions on their next request.

The settings page edits the signed-in person only: name, time zone, email, and password. There is no appearance control. The time zone must be an IANA name. Changing the email or the password requires the current password. A name or time zone change does not. A rejected save writes nothing and sends no mail. A password change updates the hash stored in the current session, so this browser stays signed in. Other sessions fail that check on their next request and are discarded. An email change does not end sessions. The password notice goes to the account's current email. The email notice goes to the old address and does not include the new address. Neither notice includes a password. The same notices are sent when a staff member changes the email or password in Django admin, and when a reset link sets the password.

django-axes locks sign-in after 5 failures for the same email and IP together. One person's misses do not lock everyone on that network. A successful sign-in clears the counter. The lock lasts one hour. The response is HTTP 429 and registration/lockout.html, which does not include the email. Axes failure logs mask the email, the password, and the IP. apps/accounts/axes.py lowercases the posted email so Ada@Example.com and ada@example.com share one counter. The test client method login() does not pass a request, which this backend requires. Tests post the sign-in form or call force_login.

/accounts/register/ returns 404, including on POST, unless SiteSettings.allow_registration is on. The switch defaults to off. When it is on, the page creates the account and signs the person in. Creating an account also creates that person's personal diary. The same is true of the admin add form and createsuperuser. How that diary is made is on Models. Staff create accounts in Django admin. The user list has a Send set-password email action. It sends the same reset message. Inactive accounts and accounts with an unusable password are skipped. The add form still requires a password; the action is how the person receives a link to replace it.

/accounts/privacy/ is public. It says who can read an entry, that this is not end-to-end encryption, and which risks remain. Backup retention and account deletion are still the phrase “to be published before launch.” The same words are in docs/help/privacy.md and accounts/privacy.html. Change them together. The footer and Settings link to the app page. The page stores nothing and writes nothing to a log.

Read this for: what .env changes, and which security headers every response sends. Source files: config/settings.py, config/client_ip.py, .env.example config/settings.py reads .env from the repository root when that file exists. A variable already set in the environment wins. .env stays untracked. Do not put real secrets in docs or in .env.example.

Variable Default when unset Effect DJANGO_SECRET_KEY none Required. The process refuses to start without it DJANGO_DEBUG false Django debug. Off unless the value is 1, true, yes, or on DJANGO_PRODUCTION false HTTPS redirect, HSTS, secure cookies, trust X-Forwarded-Proto: https from the proxy, and the SMTP mailer when DJANGO_EMAIL_BACKEND is empty DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS empty Comma-separated hosts. The test runner adds testserver when it is missing POSTGRES_DB pebble Database name POSTGRES_USER pebble Database user POSTGRES_PASSWORD empty Database password. Compose uses pebble when this is unset. Django has no default POSTGRES_HOST localhost Database host POSTGRES_PORT 5432 Host port published by Compose, and the port Django uses DJANGO_EMAIL_BACKEND empty Mail backend. Empty means SMTP in production, Gmail SMTP in development when the three fields below are set, and the console otherwise DJANGO_EMAIL_HOST empty SMTP host. Gmail is smtp.gmail.com DJANGO_EMAIL_PORT 587 SMTP port DJANGO_EMAIL_USE_TLS true STARTTLS. Use DJANGO_EMAIL_USE_SSL=true instead for port 465, and leave this false DJANGO_EMAIL_HOST_USER empty SMTP username. For Gmail, the account address DJANGO_EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD empty SMTP password. For Gmail, an app password. Stays in .env DJANGO_DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL the host user, or Pebble Diary <noreply@localhost> From address. Gmail accepts the account address USE_TZ is on. The project time zone is UTC. A user's own timezone is a field on the user, not an environment variable. A normal session lasts 14 days from the last response (SESSION_COOKIE_AGE and SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST). Password-reset links expire after one hour (PASSWORD_RESET_TIMEOUT). Sign-in throttling is on Authentication. The production check from the repository root: DJANGO_DEBUG=false DJANGO_PRODUCTION=true DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=example.com python manage.py check --deploy Gunicorn is gunicorn config.wsgi:application. It is not how local development runs. WhiteNoise serves static files. Outside production it uses Django's finders, so an app file such as apps/diary/static/diary/autosave.js is served without collectstatic. Production collects files into staticfiles/ and does not use the finders.

EMAIL_BACKEND is DJANGO_EMAIL_BACKEND when that variable is set. Otherwise production uses SMTP. Development uses SMTP when DJANGO_EMAIL_HOST, DJANGO_EMAIL_HOST_USER, and DJANGO_EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD are all set, and prints mail to the console when any of them is empty. Password reset and the change notices use that backend. The messages are on Authentication. Development mail is a Gmail account: host smtp.gmail.com, port 587, TLS. The password is a Google app password, created in the Google account under Security. Restart runserver after changing .env. A reset link uses the address you opened in the browser, so a link sent from this Mac points at 127.0.0.1.

Every response from the home page sends: Content-Security-Policy with default-src, script-src, style-src, font-src, img-src, connect-src, form-action, and base-uri set to 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'. The policy has no unsafe-inline and no unsafe-eval. Referrer-Policy: same-origin X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff X-Frame-Options: DENY Session and CSRF cookies are SameSite=Lax. The session cookie is HttpOnly. A shared-device sign-in leaves the session cookie without an expiry date. DJANGO_PRODUCTION also turns on SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT, secure session and CSRF cookies, and HSTS for one year with subdomains and preload. It treats X-Forwarded-Proto: https as a secure request, which is how the homelab proxy tells Django that TLS already ended. Leave it off for runserver. config/client_ip.py returns REMOTE_ADDR. The sign-in lock uses that address, so a client cannot pick a different one by sending a forwarded-for header. django-axes uses that callable. How the Content Security Policy constrains templates is on HTMX and templates.

Read this for: publishing a new image and running it on the homelab. Source files: Dockerfile, .github/workflows/image.yml, docker-compose.yml, .env.example The running copy is Unraid. Dockhand starts docker-compose.yml. The app container is pebble-diary, from ghcr.io/safeskies-23/pebblediary:latest. Postgres 17 is pebble-diary-postgres. A push to main builds that image and tags it latest and the commit id. A push to develop does not. The workflow logs in to ghcr.io with the token GitHub creates for that run. Dockhand uses a separate registry login. The image does not contain .env. The image runs collectstatic while it is built, with production mode on, so the static manifest exists. The app container runs python manage.py migrate and then Gunicorn on port 8000. Migrate applies pending migrations and leaves a current database unchanged. Pulling the image does not do this. Redeploy the stack with Pull images so Dockhand replaces the app container. The app service sets DJANGO_PRODUCTION true. TLS ends at the reverse proxy on the proxy network, and the app container still speaks HTTP. Point the proxy at http://pebble-diary:8000, pass the original Host, and set X-Forwarded-Proto to https. Django then treats the request as secure, redirects plain HTTP to HTTPS, and sends HSTS for one year including subdomains. The allowed hosts in the example env are localhost, 127.0.0.1, and pebblediary.com. The image with this behavior is the one built after this change. Registration is off. There is no default account. The first account was created inside the container: docker exec -it pebble-diary python manage.py createsuperuser The command asks for an email, a display name, and a password. The email is the sign-in name. Postgres is published on 127.0.0.1 only. The app reaches it at host postgres on the Compose network internal. The stack also joins an external Docker network named proxy, which must already exist. The host folder /mnt/user/appdata/pebble-diary is mounted at /postgresql/data. Postgres stores its files at /var/lib/postgresql/data, so that folder is not the database. The data for the running copy is inside the Postgres container. Recreating pebble-diary-postgres drops it. An update is three moves: Commit on develop. Merge develop into main and push main. Wait until Actions is green. In Dockhand, redeploy the stack with Pull images. Production mode also selects the SMTP mailer when DJANGO_EMAIL_BACKEND is empty. Homelab mail is not configured, so password reset on that copy still has nowhere to send a message. The backup retention window and a restore drill are not part of this copy.

Read this for: creating and editing an entry, autosave, the browser draft, and the revision check. Source files: apps/diary/services/entries.py, apps/diary/views.py, apps/diary/forms.py, apps/diary/templates/diary/entry_form.html, apps/diary/static/diary/autosave.js, templates/base.html Fields are on Models. Who may read, edit, or delete is on Permissions.

create_entry stores one row and one membership per chosen diary. The text must contain a non-whitespace character, or nothing is stored. The request must name at least one diary the person may add to. A diary they cannot read returns 404. A diary they can read but may not add to returns 403. An omitted date is today in that person's timezone. The submitted time is timezone-aware and later edits do not change it. update_entry is only for the current owner. It stores the new text and the posted diary list, and it stores a posted date when one was sent. A blank date leaves the referenced date as it is. The text is stored as submitted, including surrounding spaces. Diaries the person cannot read stay on the entry. The revision has to match the saved row. The save then increments it by one. Text, date, and diaries all wait on that check, so a stale form cannot change any of them. A mismatched or missing revision raises RevisionConflict before any write. The form is shown again with the submitted text, date, and diaries, and a link to reload the saved entry. An autosave response is JSON {"state": "conflict"} with status 409 and does not include the text. The service does not log the text. processing_instructions is not read or written. It stays empty.

The editor loads diary/autosave.js. There is no build step and no inline script. The script waits until typing has paused for one second, then sends the text, date, diaries, revision, an editor id, and a client write number. It keeps one request in flight. A response is applied only when its write number is the newest one this page sent. Blank or whitespace-only text is not sent. The server still rejects it and creates nothing. The first confirmed save creates the entry. There is no server draft row. The browser then replaces the address with /entries/<id>/, the heading becomes Edit entry, the date hint changes to keeping the saved day, and later saves go to /entries/<id>/autosave/. POST /entries/autosave/ is the create. GET on either address returns 405. A repeated create with the same editor id and write number returns the entry already stored and does not insert another. A repeated update with that same pair returns the stored row and does not change it. A lower write number from the same editor changes nothing, even if it sends the current revision. A different editor is judged only by the revision, so another tab or device is a conflict rather than a silent overwrite. The page shows one of these states, in text and in color: Saving, Saved, Offline (will retry), Conflict, and Error. Offline retries when the browser is back online. Conflict leaves the typed text in the box and offers Load the saved entry and Copy your text. Error is a validation failure, such as no diary or blank text, and the response message does not include the entry text. While the page differs from the last confirmed save, closing or leaving it asks the browser to confirm. A normal session also writes a browser draft to IndexedDB as the person types. The record is keyed by that person and the entry (or new). It expires after 14 days, which is the same length as a normal session. A confirmed save deletes it. Opening the editor offers to restore a draft whose text, date, or diaries differ from the form. This is a shared device renders data-drafts="off", and that session does not write a draft. Signing out loads the sign-in page with data-clear-drafts, and the script deletes this browser's draft database. The draft is plaintext any script on this origin can read. It is not a saved entry, and it is not in the database.

/entries/new/ and /entries/<id>/ use diary/entry_form.html. The diary boxes on a new entry start from that person's defaults. ?date=YYYY-MM-DD fills the date. Anything else leaves it blank. The same form edits an entry the person owns. Someone who can read it but does not own it sees the text and, when allowed, delete. They do not get the editor. Deleting redirects to that entry's day. Save entry still posts the form when the script does not run. With the script, that button saves immediately through the same autosave path. Reading a day is on HTMX and templates.

Read this for: what every page extends, how the day page swaps its panel, how data-theme and data-mode are set, and what the Content Security Policy forbids. Source files: templates/base.html, templates/403.html, templates/404.html, templates/500.html, apps/diary/views.py, apps/diary/urls.py, apps/diary/templates/diary/day.html, apps/diary/templates/diary/browse.html, apps/diary/templates/diary/month.html, apps/diary/templates/diary/raw.html, apps/diary/templates/diary/diary_view.html, config/theme.py, static/js/theme.js, static/css/themes.json, static/css/app.css, static/js/htmx.min.js, apps/diary/static/diary/autosave.js, config/settings.py Every normal page extends templates/base.html. The 500 page does not, because it has to render when the usual context is unavailable. It hardcodes the same light-mode attributes and loads the stylesheet only.

base.html loads static/js/theme.js in the head before static/css/app.css. HTMX is a self-hosted file at the end of the body, static/js/htmx.min.js. The editor script is diary/autosave.js, also a file. A signed-out page sets data-clear-drafts on the body so that script deletes this browser's drafts. There is no inline script and no inline style. The htmx-config meta tag sets includeIndicatorStyles to false, so HTMX does not inject a style element. Indicator styles, when a screen needs them, go in app.css. The body sets hx-headers so HTMX requests send X-CSRFToken. The day page is the screen that reads request.htmx. The write page is an ordinary form. A normal form also includes its own {% csrf_token %}. There is no inline event handler. A skip link points at the main landmark. The header shows the wordmark. A signed-in person also gets a Pages nav (Write, Diaries, Settings) and a sign-out button. The footer links to /accounts/privacy/. Diary text uses entry-text, which keeps line breaks and stops at 65 characters. templates/403.html extends the base template and says the person cannot do that. It is the response when a member lacks an action. The 500 page does not extend the base template, so it has no footer. It shows the wordmark as text. Primary buttons use the accent fill. Sign out, and the editor's conflict and restore actions, use quiet. Delete uses danger. Empty copy uses empty. A conflict and a newer local copy use notice. Form errors are the field's error list, in words and in the error color. Settings shows Saved after a change. The app does not animate.

/ redirects to /d/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ for today in the signed-in person's timezone. The path uses an isodate converter in apps/diary/urls.py. A date that is not a real calendar day, such as February 31, is 404. The page opens in Diary view. ?view=raw is Raw. Any other view value is 404. ?month=YYYY-MM shows that month's grid while keeping the selected day. A missing month is the day's own month. A month that is not YYYY-MM is 404. ?diary=<id> limits the entries, the calendar marks, and the list of days to one diary the person can read. Any other id is 404. Omitting it shows every readable diary. Diary view shows that day's entries as separate paragraphs, oldest submission first. The text is escaped and is not rewritten. Raw view lists the same entries with the submission time in the person's timezone, the diaries they can see, and Edit when they are the current owner. A day with nothing to show says so, and Write for this day opens /entries/new/?date=<that day>. A date query that is not a real day is ignored, and the editor falls back to blank, which means today. The month grid starts on Sunday. A day with an entry has a dot and the words "has entries" in its accessible name. Previous month, Next month, and Today keep the view and the diary filter. Days with entries lists every such day, newest first. That list is not paged. #browse is boosted, so those links swap that region and push the URL. Write for this day and Edit are not boosted. While a boosted request is in flight, the panel shows Loading. Those indicator rules live in app.css, because the HTMX config turns indicator styles off. A normal request, and a history restore (HX-History-Restore-Request), return diary/day.html. An HTMX request returns diary/browse.html, including a title element that HTMX lifts into the document title. Both responses send Vary: HX-Request. Who may see an entry is on Permissions. Saving one is on Entries and autosave.

static/css/themes.json lists one theme, paper-moss ("Warm Paper & Moss"), with modes ["light"]. It is the default. config/theme.py is a context processor. It sets: data-theme to paper-moss data-color-preference to the signed-in user's appearance, or system when nobody is signed in data-mode to that preference when the theme has designed it, otherwise light data-modes to the designed modes, comma-separated. Today that is light static/js/theme.js runs before the stylesheet. When the preference is system, it follows prefers-color-scheme only among data-modes. The theme has no dark mode, so the script leaves the page in light mode and does not subscribe to later system changes. A stored preference of dark also stays light until that mode exists. app.css opens with the Source Sans 3 faces, then one block, html[data-theme="paper-moss"][data-mode="light"], that defines every semantic token. Below the /* components */ marker, color properties use those variables. The layout test fails a literal color under that marker. The docs site uses the same light values in sites/pebble-diary/src/css/custom.css. Its color-mode switch is off until a dark palette exists. CopperDraw's stylesheet stays in sites/copper-draw/.

The policy is in Configuration. It allows scripts, styles, fonts, and images from this origin only. A new screen keeps that policy: Do not add an inline script, an inline event handler, or an inline style. Do not load a font, script, or image from another origin. Keep HTMX's injected indicator styles off. The 500 page loads no script, so a failure still has no inline-script exception.

Read this for: which directory owns a new file, and which of those directories exist today. Source files: manage.py, config/, apps/accounts/, apps/diary/, templates/, static/, tests/, docs/ This repository has no package.json and no website/ directory. Node dependencies stay in the shared Docusaurus app. manage.py requirements.txt .env.example Dockerfile .dockerignore docker-compose.yml .github/workflows/image.yml README.md AGENT_CONTEXT.md config/ apps/accounts/ apps/diary/ templates/ static/ tests/ docs/ .vscode/tasks.json .cursor/rules/

config/ holds settings, root URLs, ASGI, WSGI, the theme context processor, and the client-IP callable. It holds no feature models. Django apps live in apps/<label>/ and are imported as apps.<label>. The label is the directory name. accounts and diary stay fixed. accounts already has a migration. A feature goes in the app that already owns its domain. Add an app only for a separate domain with its own models, screens, and rules, and say why. Being new is not a reason. Everything a feature owns stays in that app: models, views, forms, services, permissions, management commands, admin, templates, static files, and tests. Services are plain modules in apps/<app>/services/. Views call them. Do not wrap services in another layer. accounts sends mail from apps/accounts/services/mail.py. Diary writes go through apps/diary/services/diaries.py. Entry writes go through apps/diary/services/entries.py. App templates live in apps/<app>/templates/<app>/. The day page is diary/day.html. Its swapped region is diary/browse.html, which includes diary/month.html, diary/raw.html, and diary/diary_view.html. The Diaries page is diary/diaries.html. The write and edit page is diary/entry_form.html. App static files live in apps/<app>/static/<app>/. The editor script is apps/diary/static/diary/autosave.js. App tests live in apps/<app>/tests.py or an apps/<app>/tests/ package. Account tests are apps/accounts/tests.py. Diary tests are apps/diary/tests.py. Root templates/ is shared chrome only: base.html, 403.html, 404.html, 500.html, partials/fields.html, and templates/registration/ for sign-in, password reset, registration, and the lockout page. Settings is apps/accounts/templates/accounts/settings.html. The privacy page is apps/accounts/templates/accounts/privacy.html. Root static/ is site-wide: css/app.css, css/themes.json, js/theme.js, js/htmx.min.js, and fonts/source-sans-3/. Root tests/ is for checks that span apps. Run them with python manage.py test tests. Read this for: the diary and entry tables, the one-owner constraint, and which account-creation paths create a personal diary. Source files: apps/diary/models.py, apps/diary/services/diaries.py, apps/diary/services/entries.py, apps/diary/signals.py, apps/accounts/models.py, apps/diary/migrations/0001_initial.py, apps/diary/migrations/0002_entry.py, apps/diary/migrations/0003_autosave_write.py

Diary stores a name and created_at / updated_at. It does not store an owner, and it has no shared flag. The owner is the membership row whose role is Owner. DiaryMembership is one row per person per diary (diary_membership_one_per_user). role is Owner, Editor, or Contributor (diary_membership_role_known). is_default marks that diary as one of that person's default destinations for a new entry. Several of one person's memberships may be default, and none may be. diary_one_owner is a partial unique constraint: at most one Owner row per diary. Creating a diary inserts that row. Admin cannot change memberships. Ownership transfer is not built. Who may read or change a diary or an entry is on Permissions. How a save works is on Entries and autosave.

User.save runs inside a transaction. A post_save receiver then creates one diary and one Owner membership with is_default set. The diary is named from the display name, as in Ada's Personal Diary. Registration, Django admin, createsuperuser, and User.objects.create_user all save a new user, so each of them gets that diary. A later save of the account does not add a diary or rename the one that exists. A diary created on the Diaries page is owned by that person and is not a default until they check it. Deleting a user deletes their memberships. A diary with no memberships left is deleted with them. A diary that still has other members is kept, and then has no owner. Nothing in the product creates that second case yet. Build plan #13 replaces it. The migration backfills one personal diary for each account that already existed.

Entry stores the current owner, the raw text, the calendar date the entry is about, the timezone-aware time it was submitted, and a revision that starts at 1. entry_raw_text_not_blank rejects blank or whitespace-only text. entry_revision_at_least_one rejects a revision below 1. autosave_editor and autosave_write remember the last autosave from one open editor so an older write from that editor cannot replace a newer one. They are not diary text. processing_instructions is an empty text column. Nothing reads or writes it. The owner link is PROTECT. Deleting an account that still owns an entry fails, so the delete cannot drop the text. Account deletion replaces that in build plan #13. EntryMembership ties one entry to one diary (entry_membership_one_per_diary). The same entry can belong to more than one diary. Deleting the entry deletes those rows.
There is no shared-diary flag and no audit table. processing_instructions is stored and unused.

Pebble Diary is a private diary for the family. You can sign in, reset a password, change your settings, keep private diaries, and write entries. After you sign in you see today.

Getting started — set a password, sign in, and sign out. Privacy — who can read an entry, and what the service can read. Day — move through days, and switch Raw and Diary. Write — write an entry, watch it save, and recover a conflict. Settings — your name, time zone, email, and password. Diaries — your personal diary, more private diaries, and defaults. Signing in — a forgotten password, too many tries, and a shared computer. Saving — Saving, Saved, Offline, Conflict, and a copy kept in the browser. Future plans — what is coming, and what is not available yet.

Saving means the page is sending what you typed. Saved means it is stored. Offline (will retry) means this page will send it when the connection returns. Leave the page open. Conflict means the entry was saved somewhere else, and your wording is still in the box. Error means it could not be saved, often because the note is blank or no diary is checked.

On your own phone or computer, reopen the editor. If a newer copy is still in this browser, the page offers to restore it. That copy lasts 14 days, and signing out removes it. On a shared device, the browser does not keep a copy. If the page was still open, it retries after the connection returns.
documents.s: I closed the page before it said Saved

documents.t: The box still has what you typed. Copy your text keeps that wording. Load the saved entry shows the wording that was saved and replaces the box. Saving does not overwrite the other copy on its own.

Check This is a shared device before you sign in. That session does not keep a copy in the browser. Choose Sign out when you are done. Signing out also removes copies this browser kept from another session.
documents.s: I am on someone else's computer

documents.t: On the sign-in page, choose Forgot your password? and enter your email. If an account uses that email, it receives a link. The page says the same thing either way. The link works once and expires after one hour.
After several wrong passwords, sign-in asks you to wait an hour. The message is the same whether or not that email has an account. A different email can still sign in.

Check This is a shared device before you sign in. The session ends when the browser closes, and the browser does not keep an unsaved copy. You can also choose Sign out in the header when you are done. Signing out removes copies this browser kept from another session.
documents.s: I am on someone else's computer

documents.t: That is what a password change does. The browser where you changed it stays signed in. If you did not change it, use Forgot your password? on the sign-in page. The account email also gets a notice when the password changes.
documents.s: I changed my password and my other device signed me out

documents.t: A notice goes to the old address. It does not include the new address. Your other browsers stay signed in.

Someone who runs Pebble Diary creates your account and sends you an email. The email has a link to set your password. The link works once and expires after one hour. If it has expired, ask for a new one from the sign-in page. Sign in with your email and password. Leave This is a shared device unchecked on a phone or computer that is yours. You stay signed in for 14 days, and each visit starts that 14 days again. Check This is a shared device on a computer other people use. You are signed out when the browser closes, and that browser does not keep an unsaved copy. Sign out is in the header. Use it when you are done on a shared computer. If you forget the password, use Forgot your password? on the sign-in page. Signing in answers the usual problems. Your name, email, time zone, and password are on Settings. A new account has one private diary. After you sign in you see today. Day explains the calendar and the two ways to read a day. Diaries in the header is where you see your diary, add another, and choose the defaults for a new entry. Diaries explains that page. Write is where you save an entry. Write explains that page. Privacy in the footer explains who can read what you write, and what the service can read. Privacy is that page.

After you sign in, you see today. Previous month and Next month change the calendar and keep the day you are reading. Today comes back to today. While the day changes, the page says Loading. A dot on a date means that day has an entry. The dot is a mark, not a color by itself, and the date's name also says that it has entries. Days with entries lists those days, newest first. Choose one to open it. Diary reads that day's entries one after another, in the order they were saved. The words stay as you wrote them. Raw shows each entry on its own, with the time, the diaries it is in, and Edit when you wrote it. Switching views keeps the same day. You can copy the address of either view. All diaries shows every diary you can read. Choose one name to hide the others for this day, the calendar, and the list. An entry that is in two of your diaries still appears once. A day with nothing written says so. Write for this day opens the editor with that date filled in. Write explains saving. Delete entry on the editor removes it from every diary it is in, then returns you to that day.

Open Diaries in the header. A new account starts with one diary, named from your name, such as Ada's Personal Diary. That diary is checked by default for a new entry. It is private. Write is where a new entry uses those checks. Create diary adds another private diary. It is not checked until you check it. Rename is there for a diary you own. The name is the label you see. Defaults for new entries is the set of diaries a new entry will use. Check one, several, or none, then Save defaults. Someone else's diary does not appear on this page.

Open Settings in the header. Privacy on that page, and in the footer, explains who can read what you write. Privacy is that explanation. Backup and deletion details are still to be published. You can change your name, your time zone, your email, and your password. The time zone is a name such as America/Los_Angeles. A new entry with no date uses today in that time zone. There is no appearance choice yet. The diary stays in light mode. Changing your email or your password asks for your current password. Changing your name or time zone does not. When you change your password, your other browsers and devices are signed out. This browser stays signed in. The account email gets a short notice. When you change your email, the notice goes to the old address. Other browsers stay signed in. The page says Saved. after a change. If something was wrong, the page keeps what you typed and does not save it.

Open Write in the header. Type in the box. The page saves on its own after you pause, and it shows Saving, then Saved. What you save is kept as you wrote it, including line breaks. A blank note is not saved. Date is optional. Leave it blank and the entry uses today in the time zone on Settings. Or pick the day the entry is about. That can be an earlier day. Diaries start from the ones you checked on Diaries. Check at least one. The same entry can be in more than one diary, and it is still stored once. Save entry saves immediately. You can also wait for Saved. Day is where you read it again. Write for this day opens this page with that date filled in. Leave the date blank on a new entry to use today. On an entry you already saved, leave the date blank to keep the saved day. Edit on the Raw view opens an entry you wrote. If the connection drops, the status says Offline (will retry). Leave the page open. When the connection returns, it saves. On a phone or computer that is yours, a copy also stays in this browser until the save is confirmed, you sign out, or 14 days pass. If you reopen the editor and that copy is newer, the page offers to restore it. On a shared device, this browser does not keep that copy. Saving answers the usual questions. If you leave the page before it says Saved, the browser asks you to confirm. If the entry was saved somewhere else, the status says Conflict. What you typed stays in the box. Load the saved entry shows what was saved. Copy your text copies what you typed so you can keep it. Delete entry removes it from every diary it is in. You can change the wording of an entry you wrote. Someone else cannot change that wording.

Pebble Diary is a private diary. This page says who can read an entry, what the service itself can read, and what is still to be published before launch. The same page is linked from the footer and from Settings.

You can read the entries in your diaries. The app does not show diary text to site staff, and a staff sign-in does not open someone else's diary. A person who is not a member of a diary gets the same “page not found” as a missing page. They do not learn that the diary exists. Sharing a diary with another person is not available yet. Until it is, an entry stays on your account.

This is not end-to-end encryption. The service reads an entry in order to save it and show it to you, including on another device. When you open the site over HTTPS, that connection is encrypted. The database is encrypted where it is stored. Encryption in transit and at rest does not stop the service, or someone who hosts the database and holds the keys, from reading entries.
documents.s: The service can read what you write

documents.t: Diary text is not sent to an external AI service. Diary text is not added to the logs used to run the site. On a phone or computer that is yours, the browser keeps a copy of an unsaved entry until the save is confirmed, you sign out, or 14 days pass. Signing in with “This is a shared device” does not keep that copy. Signing out removes copies this browser kept.
documents.s: What the app does not do with the text

documents.t: How long a backup keeps an entry, and how account deletion will work, are to be published before launch. You cannot delete an account from the app yet.

The service can read what you write. This is not end-to-end encryption. Someone with your unlocked, signed-in phone or computer can read your diaries. Sign out on a shared computer. Changing your password signs out other sessions. An operator, or the company that hosts the database, can read content if they have the data or the keys. Access to that is limited. It cannot be ruled out. There is no second sign-in factor. Your password, and the email account that can reset it, are what keep other people out. A reset link works once and expires after one hour.
Sign-in, settings, private diaries, writing an entry, and reading a day are in the app. Writing saves while you type. Privacy explains who can read an entry. The rest of this list is not in the app.
